problem.title: Coherent information of random sub-unitary channels

question.summary: No complete degradability, coherent-information or capacity analysis is known for the intended normalized cyclic sub-unitary family.
question.importance: The cyclic low-rank Kraus structure offers a controlled testbed for degradability and superadditive coherent information. A solution would give exact capacities for a nontrivial noisy-channel family.
question.unresolved: Classify degradability and determine coherent-information additivity and quantum capacity for the intended random sub-unitary channel class.

sourceRefs.statedTitle: Properties of coherent information of random sub-unitary channels; degradability and additivity

claims.title: Bounded-Schmidt-rank tools address only the surrounding structure
claims.text: Sub-unitary and generic-channel methods provide context, but no full theorem for this cyclic family.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

editorial.interpretation: The printed Kraus formula is not trace preserving. The research question is interpreted for the intended normalized cyclic family with varying input supports.

notices.title: Four archived channel questions need a corrected formula
notices.text: The printed random sub-unitary Kraus operators are not trace preserving. The four entries use the intended normalized cyclic family and state that interpretation explicitly.
